author: conductor
title: Adopt librarian + debugger as a marked conductor-direct agent class; the class marking is load-bearing
statement:
Sterling's agent roster now holds TWO classes, and the distinction is STRUCTURAL, not documentation:
- `pipeline` (9 agents) — dispatched inside a run, carry `handoff_write`/`agent_exit`, slice-guarded and cap-counted by H8.
- `conductor_direct` (librarian, debugger) — dispatched outside a run, hold NO `agent_exit`/`handoff_write` (both are run-scoped and refused with `no active run`), and report their signal as the FIRST LINE OF FINAL TEXT.

The marking lives in `agent-templates/registry.json` as a `class` field (registries first, invariant 3), is mirrored by `AGENT_CLASS` in packages/schemas, and is CONSUMED by H8 via the derived `PIPELINE_AGENT_TYPES`. It is load-bearing by construction: a totality test asserts the mirror matches the registry in both directions, rejects unknown class values, and asserts conductor-direct agents are absent from the H8 guard set.

This replaces a REGRESSION introduced earlier in the same session: h8-dispatch-cap.mjs derived its guarded set from `Object.keys(AGENT_MODEL_KEY)` — the whole roster — so registering the two conductor-direct agents silently enrolled them in pipeline slice-guarding and cap-counting. A mid-run dispatch of either was denied with a knowledge-slice message meaningless for a conductor-direct clerk, and consumed pipeline cap slots. Scoped to `machine_state === 'running'` (h8:72), but that is exactly the mid-run debugger reach.

Wiring: the librarian is wired into `skills/drain` — classification (co-tenant vs substantive, already-paid vs behind) stays with the CONDUCTOR; only the resulting mechanical writes may be dispatched, and delegation is explicitly OPTIONAL (P1: for one or two items inline is cheaper). `skills/debug` was deliberately NOT rewired: root-causing is judgment work and delegating the evidence chain can cost the conductor context it needs.

Debugger instrumentation: the template documents the `node --test <scratchpad>/probe.mjs` idiom rather than a FULL/BOUNDED mode premised on a project declaring a probe command. That premise was FALSE (research_finding 08893fc0): `node --test <file>` executes top-level code and is allowlisted by default, so the per-project `probe:` opt-in is redundant. An agent that wrongly believes it cannot gather evidence narrates an unfalsified hypothesis — false-blocked is the worst output of a root-causer.

Verified: 509 tests / 508 pass / 0 fail; `npm run check` clean at 11 templates; librarian reaches the store in BOTH launcher modes in sterling-main AND Comsoft; the corrected debugger wrote `<scratchpad>/probe.mjs` and executed it via `node --test`, reporting EXEC=YES.

alternatives_rejected.option: Leave the two agents unmarked in the registry (the as-built state before the council)
alternatives_rejected.reason: Already misfiring, not merely untidy: H8 derives its guard set from AGENT_MODEL_KEY's keys, so an unmarked conductor-direct agent is silently treated as a pipeline agent. 'Unmarked' was not a neutral choice — it was a live regression. Black and green independently converged on the marking having to be load-bearing rather than a decorative field.

alternatives_rejected.option: A decorative `class` field in registry.json that nothing consumes
alternatives_rejected.reason: Documentation that drifts. A field no code reads cannot fail a test, so it would have gone stale the first time an agent was added — the same class of failure as the MCP prefix, which survived a full day because nothing mechanical checked it.

alternatives_rejected.option: Relax agent_exit's run-scope so conductor-direct agents can emit structured signals (green's round-1 proposal)
alternatives_rejected.reason: Rejected by black and withdrawn: agent_exit writes to a run record, and loosening its scope to accommodate two agents weakens a run-lifecycle invariant (P4) to solve a reporting-format problem. The first-line-of-text convention is weaker but costs no invariant. Whether the platform offers a supported structured exit outside a run is an open research question, not a thing to invent.

alternatives_rejected.option: Keep the debugger's FULL/BOUNDED mode and the per-project probe opt-in
alternatives_rejected.reason: Built on a falsified premise (research_finding 08893fc0) — it would ship an agent that declines probes it is permitted to run. The keep-or-solve decision the user made was sound given the information available at the time; the information was wrong, so the decision was revisited rather than honored mechanically.

rationale: Adoption requested by the user after both agents proved themselves in the Comsoft project; run conductor-direct with intake by the user's choice. The class marking and the debugger correction both come from the six-hats council (run wf_0d90ab18-436, 16 agents, 0 errors) run post-hoc at the user's request — 'better safe than sorry - would suck if we didnt actually make sterling better'. Every load-bearing council claim was verified directly before being acted on: the `node --test` execution fact by live probe, the H8 coupling by reading h8:13 and h8:72. P3 favors the registry-derived class over a second hand-maintained list; P8 keeps classification with the conductor and clerking with the cheap agent.
